where: Section 1, the sentence beginning "Read the sign"
problem: The condition is garbled: "If Z crossed:" is not a condition a student can follow, and the next clause jumps straight to the crossed case without saying Z < D. Since the whole sign convention of the chapter hinges on this sentence, a reader can easily take away the wrong rule.
fix: Read the sign. If Z < D, the disparity is crossed: the left eye's copy sits to the right of the right eye's copy, so the eyes converge in front of the screen and the point appears in front of the glass.

problem: "Two frames for the same eye are one slot apart on either side" is ambiguous — it can be read as 8.33 ms, and "on either side" has no clear referent.
fix: Consecutive frames for the same eye have the other eye's slot between them, so the interval is 2 × 8.33 = 16.67 ms, which is 1/60 s.
